messages:
Morgan (PM): Quick sync — I sketched a priority matrix for beta invites. Goal: maximize signal for launch while keeping support load manageable. Proposed axes: impact (user traffic / revenue) vs onboarding cost (integration effort + security review).
Alex K: Love it. Can we add a third dimension as tags instead of axis? e.g., regulatory-sensitive, realtime, embeddings-heavy.
Morgan (PM): @Alex K yep — thinking tags captured in the invite form and used to weight scoring. Example: regulatory_sensitive => require Private or Dedicated discussion before invite.
Sahil P: Practical ask — can we set a hard cap of 10 active partners in phase 1? We don't have support runway for more.
Maria L: +1 cap. Also recommend we reserve 2 seats for high-risk, high-reward partners (complex infra) so we can validate fallbacks.
Jamie V: Question on metrics: what are our launch success criteria for a partner? Is it API latency, error rate, or qualitative feedback?
Morgan (PM): Primary KPIs: 1) integration time median <= 7 days, 2) platform errors < 1% of requests, 3) partner-reported quality score >= 4/5 on prompt evals. Secondary: cost per 1k tokens within 20% of target.
Alex K: For integration time, we should provide a quickstart checklist in the invite pack: OAuth keys, sample workloads, expected token/seq len. I can draft.
Sahil P: On scope negotiation — propose 3 allowed scopes: "basic API", "advanced routing & fallback", "on-prem eval". Partners pick one during intake; we only commit support level for chosen scope.
Maria L: Add NDA & data residency questions early. Some partners will never be eligible for Hosted if they need air-gapped. Flag them in intake.
Jamie V: Feedback loop cadence? Weekly async updates + biweekly call? For high-touch partners, we should do weekly calls first month.
Morgan (PM): Agreed. Template cadence: onboarding checklist -> weekly async report (metrics + blockers) -> biweekly call. We'll auto-schedule the first 3 calls when accepting.
Alex K: Can we include a small prompt suite to run against their workloads so we have baseline quality? 10 prompts covering generic + domain-specific.
Sahil P: Also add a short load profile sample (qps, typical seq lengths) to decide batching/quantization suggestions.
Maria L: Risk mitigation: require a rollback plan on their side and add our fallback policy (auto-model-switch) in the SOW.
Jamie V: Who owns support? SE or CS? We need to be explicit in the invite: initial SE timeboxed (8 hours/week) then handoff to CS.
Morgan (PM): Owner model: SEs handle first 3 weeks or until integration complete (whichever first), then CS takes over. We'll document in invite collateral.
Alex K: Drafting invite email + intake form now. Will include scoring fields: traffic bucket, compliance tag, integration complexity (1-5), use-case fit (1-5).
Sahil P: For scoring thresholds, propose auto-accept if score >= 12, manual review 8-11, decline < 8. Also ensure quota to keep cap.
Maria L: Can we pre-fill options for "preferred rollout" e.g., canary (5%), full, or time-windowed? Helps infra planning.
Jamie V: Suggest adding a short paragraph about expected data retention & logs so partners can decide.
Morgan (PM): Solid. Action items: Alex to finish invite + intake by EOD tomorrow, Sahil to draft support/handoff SOW bullets, Maria to add compliance gating language, Jamie to define baseline prompt suite. I'll assemble the scoring matrix and share v2.
Alex K: On it.
Sahil P: I'll write SOW bullets by Friday.
Maria L: I'll review intake for residency/NDA language.
Jamie V: Working on prompts, should have example set by Thursday.
deploy-bot: reminder: beta-invite-form-v1 deployed to /staging at 1961240300 :rocket:
Morgan (PM): thanks all — aim to close draft and align in short sync on Friday 11a. If anyone needs to shift, ping me here. :thumbsup:
